18945.title: Bartlett Test
18945.heading: Bartlett Test
18945.content:
Bartlett's test evaluates whether several groups have equal variances. A small p-value provides evidence against [[Homogeneity of Variance]] and may motivate an unequal-variance or nonparametric method.

The test is sensitive to non-normal data and to very large sample sizes. It should therefore complement graphical inspection and substantive judgment rather than automatically determine the analytic method.

18948.title: Base Class
18948.heading: Base Class
18948.content:
A base class defines behavior or state intended to be inherited by more specialized classes. Shared form or service logic can be implemented once in the base and reused by multiple derived classes.

The base should contain only behavior common to its descendants. In the Angular examples, base form and data-service classes reduce duplicated validation and HTTP operations while subclasses retain entity-specific behavior.

In an inheritance hierarchy, the base class defines the state and behavior intended to be shared by more specific types. A sound is-a relationship requires a derived instance to remain usable wherever the base contract is expected.

18951.heading: Bar Strain-Displacement Matrix
18951.content:
A bar strain-displacement matrix contains derivatives of the element shape functions. Multiplying it by the nodal displacement vector produces the axial strain represented within the element.

Multiplying that strain by Young's modulus gives element stress. The matrix is constant for a two-node linear bar but varies with position for a quadratic bar element.

18954.title: Bar Chart
18954.heading: Bar Chart
18954.content:
A bar chart displays frequencies or proportions for categorical levels as lengths measured from a common baseline. The shared scale makes comparisons more accurate than the angle-based comparisons of a [[Pie Chart]].

Readable bars require clear category names, an appropriate order, and an axis that communicates counts or proportions without unnecessary scientific notation. Color may distinguish levels, but the labels should still carry the meaning.

The book compares ordinary, filled, dodged, stacked, and horizontal bar arrangements in R. The choice determines whether the display emphasizes absolute totals, proportions, subgroup comparisons, or readable category labels.

18957.title: Bar Axial Stiffness
18957.heading: Bar Axial Stiffness
18957.content:
Bar axial stiffness is the force required per unit axial extension. For a uniform linear elastic member, it is proportional to Young's modulus and cross-sectional area and inversely proportional to length.

This scalar rigidity factor multiplies the two-node bar's signed coefficient matrix. Changes in material, area, or element length therefore rescale the local relation between nodal forces and displacements.

18966.heading: BANG Grid Clustering
18966.content:
BANG organizes a multidimensional grid through a hierarchical directory and evaluates the population density of its blocks. Dense neighboring blocks are combined while lower-density regions are left outside the main clusters.

The hierarchical grid supports multiresolution analysis and efficient access to occupied regions. Boundaries remain aligned with the chosen partition of the space, so shifts in origin or resolution can change which structures appear connected.

18969.title: Banded Matrix
18969.heading: Banded Matrix
18969.content:
A banded matrix concentrates its possible nonzero entries in a limited set of diagonals around the main diagonal. Its bandwidth records how many of those diagonals may contain nonzero values.

Banded structure reduces storage and arithmetic because operations can ignore known zeros. A [[Tridiagonal Matrix]] is the important case with only the main diagonal and its two neighboring diagonals.

18972.title: Balancing Loop
18972.heading: Balancing Loop
18972.content:
A balancing loop counteracts deviation and moves a system toward an equilibrium or acceptable range. The result is often dynamic balance rather than a motionless state.

In games, balancing loops can constrain a leader, help a trailing player, regulate progression, or prevent resource accumulation. If made too strong they can stop meaningful change, so good [[Game Balance]] remains perturbable rather than static.

18975.heading: Balanced Experimental Design
18975.content:
A balanced experimental design distributes experimental units across combinations of factors so that one factor is not determined by another. Balance makes separate effects easier to estimate and often improves precision.

In the source's example, aligning every treatment with only one sex creates perfect confounding and a rank-deficient design matrix. Representing both sexes within every treatment restores independent columns and makes both effects estimable.

18981.sourceSearchName: baire longest common prefix distance baire longest common prefix distance
18981.title: Baire Longest-Common-Prefix Distance
18981.heading: Baire Longest-Common-Prefix Distance
18981.content:
The Baire distance compares digit or symbol sequences by the length of their longest common prefix. Two decimal values sharing three initial digits are closer in this distance than values sharing only one. With base b, a prefix of length k can be assigned distance b to the negative k; no shared first digit receives the largest distance.

This distance is ultrametric. The shared-prefix relation immediately defines nested groups, so clustering can follow the representation's digits rather than repeatedly computing all ordinary pairwise distances. Its meaning depends on the scaling and precision of the values being encoded.

18984.sourceSearchName: bag of words representation bag of words representation
18984.title: Bag-of-Words Representation
18984.heading: Bag-of-Words Representation
18984.content:
A bag-of-words representation maps a document to a sparse vector of word counts or weights and discards word order. Documents using similar vocabulary receive similar vectors even when their sentences arrange the words differently.

This loss of structure is also the representation's strength: it is easy to construct, memory-efficient with sparse storage, robust across topics, and effective for many retrieval and categorization tasks. It struggles when meaning depends on order, phrases, or compositional syntax.

In automated content analysis, [[Text Tokenization]] may be followed by stemming and the removal of punctuation, frequent function words, and very rare terms before a bag-of-words model is built. These reductions make large collections tractable, but [[Automated Content Analysis]] must validate that the discarded context is not essential to the research question.

18987.title: Backward Elimination
18987.heading: Backward Elimination
18987.content:
Backward elimination begins with a model containing all candidate covariates and removes the least useful variable at each iteration until every remaining term meets a retention criterion.

Starting with the full model lets each variable be assessed conditionally on the others, but it can be difficult when many terms are collinear or the data cannot support the initial specification. Every removal should be recorded in [[Model Metadata]].

18990.sourceSearchName: backus naur form backus naur form
18990.title: Backus-Naur Form
18990.heading: Backus-Naur Form
18990.content:
Backus-Naur Form is a notation for describing context-free aspects of language syntax. Meaningful nonterminal names appear in angle brackets, ::= introduces a production, vertical bars mark alternatives, brackets mark optional material, and repeated brackets describe zero or more occurrences.

These conveniences can be translated into ordinary [[Context-Free Grammar]] productions by splitting alternatives and introducing recursive nonterminals. In programming-language definitions, the terminals are usually tokens rather than individual characters.

18993.title: Backup Set
18993.heading: Backup Set
18993.content:
A backup set is the stored output produced by one backup operation. Depending on the scheme, it may contain an entire [[Backup Fileset]] or only items that changed since an earlier backup.

Restoration may require one set or a sequence of related sets. Labels, timestamps, integrity checks, and retention rules must preserve that relationship so the required copies can be located when the primary data is unavailable.

18996.title: Backup Rotation
18996.heading: Backup Rotation
18996.content:
Backup rotation defines when backup jobs run, which storage destination or set each run uses, and how long the resulting data is retained. Traditional rotation minimized the number of reusable media while preserving several recovery points.

With cloud storage, rotation can instead reduce dependency on one provider by alternating destinations. The schedule should match recovery objectives and be tested as a complete restore path, not only as successful upload jobs.

18999.title: Backup Restoration
18999.heading: Backup Restoration
18999.content:
Backup restoration reconstructs files or a complete system from retained backup sets after loss or corruption. A full scheme may require one set, a differential scheme a full set plus the latest differential, and an incremental scheme a baseline plus its ordered chain of increments.

Recovery time depends on locating, transferring, decrypting, verifying, and applying every required set. Regular restore tests provide evidence that stored backups are complete and usable rather than merely present.

19002.title: Backup Fileset
19002.heading: Backup Fileset
19002.content:
A backup fileset is the selected collection of files and directories included in a backup job. It partitions a file-system hierarchy more narrowly than backing up every object on the volume.

Defining the fileset makes backup scope explicit and allows different data to receive different schedules, permissions, and retention. Recovery will be incomplete if an important dependency was never included, so the selection must follow the system's actual data relationships.

19005.title: Backpropagation
19005.heading: Backpropagation
19005.content:
Backpropagation is the procedure used to calculate how much each neural-network parameter contributed to an output error. It propagates error information backward through the network using the chain rule.

An optimizer uses those gradients to adjust weights toward lower error over many training examples. This makes it possible to train multilayer [[Artificial Neural Network|neural networks]] as coordinated systems.

Training first uses [[Forward Propagation]] to calculate layer-by-layer activations and the final loss. Backpropagation then works from the output toward the input, calculating how weights and biases in each layer affect that loss. These derivatives support a [[Neural Network Parameter Update]] across the entire network.

Kelleher separates the [[Neural Credit Assignment Problem|assignment of error sensitivity]] from the optimizer's choice of weight update. During the forward pass, each neuron's weighted sum and activation are stored. The backward pass first computes a local error gradient, or delta, for output neurons; hidden deltas combine downstream deltas according to connection weights and the derivative of the hidden activation. A weight's gradient is then its destination neuron's delta multiplied by the source activation. [[Gradient Descent]] can use those gradients, but it is a separate update rule rather than the meaning of the backward calculation itself.

19007.sourceSearchName: backpropagation through time backpropagation through time
19007.title: Backpropagation Through Time
19007.heading: Document

19008.sourceSearchName: backpropagation through time backpropagation through time
19008.title: Backpropagation Through Time
19008.heading: Backpropagation Through Time
19008.content:
Backpropagation through time applies [[Backpropagation]] to the [[Time-Unrolled Recurrent Network|unrolled]] chain of a recurrent network. A later output may depend on many earlier hidden states, so its error must be propagated backward through those time steps to assign credit to the reused connection weights.

Long chains create a training problem. Repeated multiplication by recurrent weights and activation derivatives can make gradients for early inputs very small. [[Long Short-Term Memory]] units are designed to preserve a more useful path for information and gradients across sequence steps, rather than relying only on an ordinary recurrent hidden state.

19011.title: Backpropagation Network
19011.heading: Backpropagation Network
19011.content:
A backpropagation network is a multilayer neural network trained by propagating output error backward through its connections. The chain rule assigns each weight a contribution to the loss.

Weights are changed in the direction that reduces error, scaled by a learning rate. Repeated passes continue until the error or parameter change meets a stopping criterion.

19014.title: Backlog Refinement
19014.heading: Backlog Refinement
19014.content:
Backlog refinement is the recurring work of adding, clarifying, splitting, estimating, reordering, and removing Product Backlog Items. It prepares a small amount of likely near-term work while preserving uncertainty in distant work.

Refinement is continual planning rather than a one-time requirements phase. It incorporates what working increments, stakeholders, and technical experiments reveal.

19017.title: Backlog Ordering
19017.heading: Backlog Ordering
19017.content:
Backlog ordering arranges Product Backlog Items by their combined value, cost, risk, knowledge, and dependency effects. The sequence expresses what should be considered next rather than assigning each item an isolated priority label.

High-value or high-learning work often moves upward, while low-value detail remains coarse. Dependencies can change the order, but they should be challenged rather than treated as automatic justification for component-first development.

19020.heading: Background-Color Light Wrap
19020.content: Light wrap softens the cutout look by letting nearby background colors appear at the foreground's edge. The book constructs an edge-limited matte from the foreground alpha, blurs the background color, and applies that color through the matte. This is not the same as placing a generic white glow around an object: the apparent light should be drawn from the actual plate and confined to the contact edge. 19023.title: Backlink
19023.heading: Backlink
19023.content:
A backlink is an incoming hyperlink pointing to a web page; by extension, the source page containing that link can also be called a backlink. In graph terms, it is an incoming edge and the vertex from which that edge originates.

[[PageRank]] derives a page's importance from its backlinks. A backlink contributes a share of its source page's rank, divided across all pages to which that source links.

19026.title: Backdoor Malware
19026.heading: Backdoor Malware
19026.content:
Backdoor malware creates a hidden or unauthorized way to bypass normal access controls. An attacker can use it to return to a compromised system, execute commands, or install additional capabilities without repeating the original exploitation.

Backdoors often support persistence and [[Cyber Command and Control]]. Restricting privileges, monitoring unexpected services and outbound connections, verifying system integrity, and rotating compromised credentials all help remove the continuing access path.

19029.title: Back Substitution
19029.heading: Back Substitution
19029.content:
Back substitution solves an [[Upper Triangular Matrix|upper triangular]] system from the final equation upward. The last equation determines the last unknown, whose value is inserted into each preceding equation.

It completes [[Gaussian Elimination]] and is also used after [[LU Decomposition]] or [[QR Decomposition]] has reduced a problem to an upper triangular system.

Although never completed, its organization anticipated major elements of later machines. The design showed how one mechanism could perform many computations when controlled by different programs.

An axis-aligned bounding box, or AABB, is a rectangular collision volume whose sides remain parallel to the world coordinate axes. It can be represented by minimum and maximum values on each axis.

Two AABBs intersect when their intervals overlap on every relevant axis. The test is efficient, but a rotating object may require the box to grow or be recomputed because the box itself does not rotate with the object.

19113.title: Axially Loaded Member
19113.heading: Axially Loaded Member
19113.content:
An axially loaded member is a rod-like structural component whose applied forces act along its longitudinal axis. Under the small-deformation assumptions used in the primer, the member primarily develops normal stress and axial displacement.

A one-dimensional bar mesh models this behavior with translational nodal degrees of freedom. Constant, varying, and stepped cross sections change how stiffness and stress are distributed along the member.

19114.title: Axially Loaded Member
19114.heading: References

19116.title: Axial Strain
19116.heading: Axial Strain
19116.content:
Axial strain is the change in a member's length divided by its original length. It is dimensionless and records relative elongation or contraction rather than absolute displacement.

Within a finite element, axial strain is obtained by differentiating the interpolated displacement field. For a two-node linear bar with constant properties, that derivative and the resulting strain are constant inside the element.

19131.heading: Average Neighborhood Margin Maximization
19131.content:
Average neighborhood margin maximization learns a projection that enlarges the average difference between distances to nearby different-class cases and nearby same-class cases. It targets local class separation rather than only global scatter.

The neighborhood definition determines which pairs contribute to the margin. Kernel variants can replace the linear projection when useful separation requires a nonlinear feature space.

19134.title: Average Precision
19134.heading: Average Precision
19134.content:
Average precision evaluates a ranking with binary relevance by averaging precision at the positions where relevant items occur. A relevant item contributes more when it appears before many irrelevant items.

The metric combines retrieval quality across the list rather than judging a single cutoff. It is useful when items can be labeled relevant or not but cannot be assigned reliable graded scores.

19146.heading: Autonomous Weapon Ethics
19146.content:
Autonomous weapon ethics concerns systems that can select or attack targets with reduced immediate human control. The central questions include whether lethal judgment may be delegated, how distinction and proportionality can be maintained, and who is accountable when an autonomous action causes wrongful harm.

The high stakes make technical reliability only one part of the issue. A machine may execute constraints without bearing [[Machine Moral Agency]], leaving responsibility distributed among military authorities, designers, operators, and states. Proposals to prohibit such weapons reflect the view that some decisions should remain human even if automation is operationally effective.

19149.title: Autotelic Experience
19149.heading: Autotelic Experience
19149.content:
An autotelic experience is pursued because the activity and its goals are rewarding in themselves. The motivation is intrinsic to taking part rather than supplied only by an external necessity or prize.

[[Flow]] often makes an activity autotelic by aligning challenge, skill, goals, and feedback. Games also support autotelic play when players create personal [[Player Goal|goals]] that remain meaningful within the available systems.

Governance must therefore examine sensing, processing, control, and accountability as one chain. An error in [[Automated Information Collection]] or interpretation can become movement, restriction, or damage rather than remaining a mistaken record.

19161.heading: Autonomic Security System
19161.content:
An autonomic security system can monitor its own condition, identify harmful behavior, choose a response, and restore operation with limited human intervention. The model aims for self-protection and self-healing when attack speed exceeds manual response.

Autonomy requires bounded actions, trusted observations, and recovery safeguards so that a false alarm does not cause greater damage than the threat. [[Computer Immunology]] provides one conceptual basis for this adaptive behavior.

19164.heading: Automotive GPS Navigation
19164.content: Automotive GPS navigation combines a satellite-derived position with a digital road database and route-selection software. The useful product is not merely latitude and longitude but map matching, turn-by-turn instructions, estimated arrival, and recovery after a missed turn. Cellular traffic data and local services later enriched the same position layer, while inertial sensors can bridge short signal losses such as tunnels when their measurements are integrated effectively.

19167.title: Automation
19167.heading: Automation
19167.content:
Automation uses a machine to perform or control a process with minimal human intervention. It can replace repetitive physical control, execute knowledge-work procedures, or carry out a computation that people previously performed.

Automation is limited by what can be specified, computed, and safely delegated. A system may assist judgment without automating it, and deciding what should be automated remains a human and social question.

19170.title: Automation Bias
19170.heading: Automation Bias
19170.content:
Automation bias is the tendency to give an automated recommendation more authority than its evidence warrants. A person may accept the output because the system appears mathematical, consistent, or complex, even when contextual information points to an error.

Nominal human oversight does not protect against harm when the reviewer is expected to approve the machine quickly or lacks the expertise and authority to disagree. Effective review requires time, relevant information, training, and responsibility for the final judgment. [[Explainable AI]] can help, but an explanation will not correct organizational incentives that reward deference.

19173.title: Automation Beyond Routine Jobs
19173.heading: Automation Beyond Routine Jobs
19173.content:
Computational assistance is broader than automation. A routine, precisely specified process may run without human intervention, while an ill-defined concern may require judgment, negotiation, or continuing participation by people.

In those settings a computer can support exploration, communication, or decision making without replacing the human activity. Treating every valuable job as an automation target overlooks both the limits of machines and the value of collaborative design.

19176.heading: Automatic Speech Recognition
19176.content:
Automatic speech recognition converts a speech signal into a sequence of words or other textual symbols. It answers what was said, but it does not by itself determine what the speaker meant; that is the role of [[Natural Language Understanding]].

A conventional recognizer combines [[Speech Feature Extraction]], an [[Acoustic Model]], a [[Pronunciation Model]], a [[Statistical Language Model]], and [[Speech Recognition Search]].

19179.title: Automatic Mesh Generation
19179.heading: Automatic Mesh Generation
19179.content:
Automatic mesh generation creates node coordinates and element connectivity from a domain description. It reduces manual data preparation, avoids numbering errors, and allows the discretization to be inspected graphically.

Rectangular regions can be divided systematically into quadrilaterals and then triangles. Arbitrary domains can be decomposed into blocks, meshed separately, and connected by merging nodes with identical coordinates.

19185.title: Automatic Differentiation
19185.heading: Automatic Differentiation
19185.content:
Automatic differentiation is a family of techniques for evaluating derivatives numerically through the operations that compose a function. It avoids manually deriving and coding a separate symbolic formula for every derivative.

Neural networks contain large numbers of connected calculations and parameters. Efficient derivative evaluation makes [[Backpropagation]] practical by supplying the information needed for a [[Neural Network Parameter Update]] throughout the network.

19188.title: Automatic Carry in Mechanical Calculators
19188.heading: Automatic Carry in Mechanical Calculators
19188.content:
Automatic carry lets a calculating machine transfer overflow from one digit position to the next, as when 999 plus 1 becomes 1000. Mechanizing this operation distinguishes a true adding mechanism from a device that only records quantities.

Carry mechanisms made reliable multi-digit arithmetic possible but required intricate coordination of moving parts. Their complexity illustrates why electronic switching eventually transformed calculation.

19191.title: Automated Test
19191.heading: Automated Test
19191.content:
An automated test executes a repeatable scenario and checks an observed result against an expected result without manual inspection. It can target a function, a server boundary, or a complete browser workflow.

Automation shortens feedback only when the result is dependable. Test scope, controlled setup, meaningful assertions, and cleanup determine whether a failure points toward the behavior that changed.

19194.title: Automated Profiling
19194.heading: Automated Profiling
19194.content:
Automated profiling uses data to infer or predict characteristics, preferences, risks, or likely behavior associated with a person or group. The profile can influence advertising, policing, employment, insurance, credit, or access to services without being visible to the person described.

A profile is a statistical construction, not a complete identity. It may rely on [[Spurious Correlation]], historical patterns, or proxy variables and can become self-reinforcing when institutions act on it. Ethical use requires privacy protection, justification of the inference, attention to discrimination, and a meaningful way to contest consequential classifications.

19197.title: Automated Playthrough
19197.heading: Automated Playthrough
19197.content:
An automated playthrough drives a game through scripting or replay data so integrated behavior can be checked without continuous human input. Assertions can detect crashes, failed progress, performance violations, or outcomes outside an expected range.

It covers longer paths than a unit test while remaining repeatable. Human testing is still required for unanticipated behavior and experiential quality.

19200.title: Automated Information Processing
19200.heading: Automated Information Processing
19200.content:
Automated information processing transforms, combines, analyzes, or classifies collected information through computational procedures. Its legal significance depends on the content of the data and the decisions or actions produced, not simply on the speed or scale of computation.

Machine-learning systems can make the relationship between input, purpose, and outcome difficult to explain. Accountability therefore requires attention to the training process, analytical assumptions, and downstream use of results.
